title: Contested case on Mahi Pono East Maui water permits
summary: The Board of Land and Natural Resources (BLNR) rejected the operator’s request for a contested case after a closed-door session, and the operator’s attorney appealed that denial in circuit court on September 11. A court-ordered contested case on the 2026 and 2027 revocable permits is moving ahead. The hearings, first set for November 4 and 5, were postponed to January 19, 2027, to allow more time for evidence and witness preparation, The Maui Daily reported on October 20. Permit applicants must show how much water they need.

timeline.text: The director was asked to look into a short online special meeting for a contested case update after October 1.
Hearings are estimated at 15 days, with a result hoped for by the end of the year.
Witness testimony will be submitted in writing, and witnesses will then face cross-examination (questions from other parties).
Open questions, including where hearings are held and whether they are streamed, will be decided after an October 1 prehearing.
The county attorney will update the board after the October 1 prehearing.
The permit applicants carry the burden to show how much water they need.
The attorney said the case is only about the 2026 and 2027 permits, not the long-term license.
Hearings are planned for Oʻahu, not Maui, but that is not yet decided.
A prehearing is set for October 1, with hearings November 4 and 5.
On September 11, the operator's attorney appealed the denial of its contested case request in circuit court.
Board of Land and Natural Resources (BLNR) rejected the operator's request for a contested case (a trial-like hearing) after an executive session (a closed-door discussion).
Mahi Pono may appeal the denial of its contested case request in court within a set number of days.
The contested case process on the revocable permits will now start.
Board of Land and Natural Resources (BLNR) unanimously let its chair appoint a hearings officer to start that contested case for 2026 and 2027 permits.
About a month ago, a judge ordered Board of Land and Natural Resources (BLNR) to hold a contested case on the revocable permits.
A community member withdrew a contested case request (a formal, trial-like hearing) so the board could vote.
An environmental court judge heard arguments on an appeal over an earlier permit and said a decision would come soon.
The vice chair said the state land board will have to issue at least one more revocable permit (a short-term permit that can be cancelled).

takePart.note: The State Board of Land and Natural Resources (the Land Board), not the County, decides these permits. A court ordered a contested case on the 2026 and 2027 permits, which works like a trial: witness testimony is submitted in writing and witnesses are cross-examined. As of the Sept. 18 ʻAha Moku o Maui Hikina meeting, hearings were set for Nov. 4 and 5, with the place and any streaming to be decided after an Oct. 1 prehearing. Check the Land Board for the current schedule.
